next_step: Finalize latency SLO language + draft Dedicated capacity proposal (8xH100 baseline)
blockers: agreement on client vs server timing windows
notes:
Account overview:
- Enterprise quant trading firm exploring Dedicated + Private for latency-sensitive inference. Primary driver: predictable p95 SLOs for trader-facing assistants and reranking for market signals.
- Wants strict measurement alignment before procurement: definitions for p50/p95/p99, difference between streaming vs non-streaming latency, and explicit client-side vs server-side timing windows.
Recent timeline / activities:
- 2026-02-10: Intro call (AE Maya) - gathered high-level reqs, confirmed compliance bar (SOC2, KMS, residency).
- 2026-02-19: Technical deep-dive with SE (Carlos) - live demo of hosted latency profiles; Coppercliff provided sample 99th percentile spike traces. (ff_2026_02_24_44109)
- 2026-03-02: Onsite perf workshop - ran synthetic load: 200 concurrent sessions, 64-token gen, measured token-emission vs total-response time. Discussed batching/caching tradeoffs. (ff_2026_03_02_78321)
- 2026-03-09: Security questionnaire returned; legal flagged data residency + retention specifics.
POC / evaluation scope:
- POC target: validate Dedicated baseline (8xH100 pool) can sustain 800 concurrent trader sessions with p95 < 120ms for non-streaming 1-token turns and steady-state token throughput >= 14k tokens/s across pool.
- Streaming SLOs: initial token (first byte) p50 < 30ms, p95 < 80ms; steady-state per-token emit p95 < 35ms.
- Non-streaming SLOs: full response latency p50/p95/p99 targets: 40ms / 120ms / 260ms for 64-token typical responses. (customer uses truncated prompts avg 48 tokens)
Measurement alignment notes (customer insisted):
- "Client-side timing includes TLS + SDK serialization" — customer wants clarity which pieces Redwood measures. They asked for: client_initiated_ts, server_ingest_ts, server_emit_first_token_ts, server_emit_last_token_ts, client_received_last_token_ts.
- Need to agree on warm vs cold starts: define warm as prior request within 5s for same model+route (KV cache hot). Cold-starts counted separately in SLA reports.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: customer requires separate SLOs and separate credit calculus. They will not accept streaming latencies being mapped to non-streaming targets.
- Sampling and statistical confidence: request Redwood provide daily histograms (1-minute buckets) + weekly p99 bootstrap confidence intervals; minimum sample size 10k requests/day for SLA compliance evaluation.
Reserved GPU planning & throughput guarantees:
- Customer prefers H100/80GB profile for baseline. Proposed reserve: 8xH100 with 2:1 concurrency headroom for autoscale bursts.
- Throughput expectations: assume model variant trimmed to 8-bit quant; measured tokens/sec per GPU ~1.8-2.2k (depending on prompt mix). Customer wants committed throughput guarantee of 14k tokens/s with vertical/horizontal scaling clauses.
SLA negotiation items (to resolve):
- Credit methodology: customer requests credits based on missed p95 minutes aggregated monthly (example: credits prorated for minutes where rolling 15-minute p95 exceeds threshold). Redwood proposed daily percentile checks instead.
- Uptime vs latency credits: customer wants combined metric (latency & availability) to trigger credits; Redwood prefers separate buckets.
- Penalty caps and escrow: customer requested breach escrow for first-year procurement.
Instrumentation & telemetry ask:
- Provide SDK hooks + server-side trace correlation id (x-request-id), expose both server and client-side timing fields in /metrics and a daily CSV dump.
- Include KV cache hit-rate, batch-size distribution, GPU utilization per node in perf reports.
Quotes & customer language:
- "We need measurable, auditable numbers—don't handwave p95." (Head of Platforms)
- "If 99th spikes during market open, we need automatic fallback to lower-cost model variant with graceful degradation." (SRE lead)
Next steps (short):
- Draft Dedicated proposal (Maya + Carlos) including: capacity plan (8xH100 baseline), measurement spec appendix, SLA credit formula, and pilot timeline. Due: 2026-03-20.
- Legal to review residency clause; follow-up call with legal week of 2026-03-15.
- POC kickoff: schedule 2-week pilot starting after contract signature.
Misc notes / risks:
- High variability at market open; requires canary routing by time-of-day.
- Customer heavy on cost-sensitivity during steady-state — Optimize recommendations (quantization + batching) will be important to hit ARR targets.
